label: One front camera
description: The simplest version: one inexpensive camera looking ahead. Turn the robot to look before moving into a new area.
capability: Live video, object recognition and visual landmarks.
limitation: One image does not directly measure distance in metres. The sides and rear are outside the view.
algorithmBody: Use a modest video stream for object recognition and known visual markers. Calibrated monocular SLAM can track visual features; wheel odometry or a known marker provides a metric reference.
mappingBody: Start with known landmarks and short supervised moves. General room navigation needs calibrated visual mapping and a measured scale; a language model looking at a picture does not provide a distance map.

label: Front + left + right
description: The same inexpensive camera at the front, left and right. See more of the room without turning the whole robot.
capability: Front and side views for object recognition and visual checks before moving.
limitation: Wider coverage does not automatically produce stereo depth. The rear remains outside the cameras’ views.
algorithmBody: Capture the front, left and right streams with stable device IDs. Process only the views needed for the next movement. These cameras are not treated as a synchronized stereo rig.
mappingBody: Use visual landmarks and camera calibration to relate each view to the robot. Overlapping views and multi-camera SLAM are a later integration task; three pictures alone do not create a depth map.

label: Stereo camera pair
description: Two forward-facing cameras on one rigid board. Their overlapping, synchronized images can be used to estimate distance.
capability: Front-facing stereo vision with a known baseline for metric depth after calibration.
limitation: Depth is computed by the Pi or home computer. Glass, blank surfaces, poor light and occlusion can leave gaps.
algorithmBody: Calibrate both lenses and their relative positions, rectify the synchronized images, then compute disparity with OpenCV StereoSGBM. With focal length f and baseline B, distance is Z = f × B / disparity.
mappingBody: After calibrating and measuring its useful range, feed valid stereo depth to RTAB-Map and Nav2. Invalid depth stays unknown. Benchmark image size, frame rate and processing time on the Pi or home computer.
